title: Several editions charge the full bid-ask spread on a one-sided conversion
what: Multiple pages derive the FX cost as amount x (ask - bid) / ask - both halves of the spread - when a customer buying USD pays only the selling side. On today's board that is 0.4186% instead of 0.2093%, i.e. about USD 20.94 extra per USD 10,000 and USD 837.43 extra per USD 400,000.
where: The full-spread convention appears on c5bf-rates.html (labelled sensitivity and delta columns), m5f19-costs.html (sensitivity column) and the 76e-verification table. The one-sided convention is used on index.html, d646, a513, b9b3, n676 and this edition.
official_sources: C01 (the board prints Buying 665.91 and Selling 668.71; the customer buys at the Selling rate only); C02 (the tariff is on top of the rate)
how_to_resolve: Decide one convention repo-wide and re-label every sensitivity column as "not the answer". This edition prices the one-sided cost and shows the full-spread column side by side in the reconciliation table so the gap is never invisible.
affects: Up to USD 20.94 per USD 10,000 and USD 837.43 per USD 400,000 of the published headline

title: No verified cost for remitting CNY and converting offshore
what: One lawful-looking route is to remit RMB and let an offshore bank or platform convert it. This session verified no official price for the offshore conversion or for the mainland remittance tariff of that product.
where: Method M03 in data/c348_methods.csv; every cost cell for M03 is BLANK.
official_sources: C06 (Art. 5 and Art. 12 set the principle); no official fee schedule was found and read
how_to_resolve: Ask two banks in writing for the mainland CNY remittance tariff, and two receiving institutions for their CNY/USD price. A test transfer of USD 100 reconciles the two.
affects: Cannot be ranked against M01 until priced

title: The U.S. receiving-bank and intermediary fees are not published
what: Every route leaves the receiving and intermediary fees blank. The repository carries a Bank of China corporate tariff (USD 15 or 25 per wire) but its applicability to personal wires was not verified, and no U.S. bank publishes a single incoming-wire price that applies to all accounts.
official_sources: C20 (inherited, not re-read); no equivalent official U.S. figure read in this pass
how_to_resolve: Ask the receiving U.S. bank for its incoming international wire fee in writing, and send one test wire to measure the landed amount against the sent amount.
affects: Typically the largest single unknown in a small transfer

title: What a personal currency gain is taxed as is the single most consequential open question
what: 26 U.S.C. 988(a)(1)(A) makes foreign currency gain ordinary. 988(e)(1) removes a personal transaction from the ordinary rule, and IRS Publication 525 (C12) says a personal gain above USD 200 is reported as a capital gain. The statutes and the IRS publication therefore point to different characters, and the difference on USD 400,000 is real: at a 37% ordinary rate the tax on USD 27,926 of gain is USD 10,333; at 15% it is USD 4,189.
where: This edition prices the capital-gain reading and states the ordinary alternative in the tax page and in every tax row
how_to_resolve: A written opinion from a U.S. tax adviser on the specific facts, or an IRS private letter ruling. Until then, plan for the capital treatment and reserve the difference.
affects: Up to about USD 6,144 on a USD 400,000 balance acquired in 2024

title: One page in the repository states the USD 50,000 convenience amount backwards
what: methods.html says "Legal $50,000 USD-equivalent per person per year (individual purchase quota)" and lists "$50,000 cap (non-salary funds)" as a drawback. SAFE states the opposite: the amount is a convenience threshold, and there is no amount limit for genuine current-account business; above the threshold the transaction simply needs documents (C05). The page also presents the quota as available to a generic individual, whereas the annual convenience amount is for domestic individuals and for holders of the PRC Foreign Permanent Resident ID (C04, C05).
where: methods.html, route table, row "1 Bank FX purchase (CNY→USD) + international wire"
official_sources: C04; C05; C03 (Art. 59 is the route for a foreign individual)
how_to_resolve: The owner of methods.html should replace the quote with the C05 wording. This session does not edit another edition's page; the correction is requested in COORDINATION.md.
affects: A reader who believes it cannot plan at all - it would wrongly cap the move at USD 50,000 a year

title: Fifteen parallel editions with no single "read this first"
what: Fifteen root-level editions publish overlapping cost tables with different boards and conventions, and the archive page does not say which one is current.
how_to_resolve: The final integration session should mark one edition canonical and banner the rest as superseded. This edition is additive and does not claim to be canonical.

title: The board moves during the day and each edition froze a different snapshot
what: The BOC board republishes intraday. This session read 665.91 / 668.71 at 20:50:05 Beijing; other editions froze 6.6606 / 6.6886 at 15:30:04, 6.6571 / 6.6851 at 10:25:02, and 6.6622 / 6.6903 on the previous day. All published costs therefore differ by a few dollars for no reason other than timing.
official_sources: C01 (Pub Time is printed on the board itself)
how_to_resolve: Quote the board timestamp beside every cost, which this edition does.
affects: Up to about USD 2 per USD 10,000 and USD 20 per USD 400,000
